newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 70-80 bcf in weekly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 70-80 bcf in weekly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 70-80 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged widely from 55 bcf to 110 bcf for the week ended Nov 29.
"It was another cool week last week, so we should see a pretty good draw," said one Houston-based trader.
Last week's draw of 66 bcf was below expectations for a 75-80 bcf decline. The four week average draw is 37 bcf.
Weekly drawdowns in November 1995 averaged 74 bcf, but cold weather last December saw stocks drained by an average of 142 bcf per week, a rate not likely to be replicated this year.

"This December, there's no way you're going to pull out as much as last year. You're going to make some inroads (in the 186 bcf stock deficit) this month," said an Eastern trader, adding concerns about lagging storage could wane this month as the gap to 1995 narrowed in coming weeks.

In the last report, Eastern stocks fell by 46 bcf to 90 percent of capacity but were still slightly above year-ago. Producing region inventories slipped 14 bcf to 68 percent full and continued to significantly lag 1995 levels at about 83 percent of capacity.

For the same week last year, total inventories fell by 73 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would leave the gap to last year roughly unchanged. In 1995, eastern storage fell by 49 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 24 bcf. Western stocks, at 68 percent in last report, stayed unchanged at 87 percent for the same year-ago week.
